html:
Mount Athos is a mountain on a long peninsula of northern Greece, and since the 900s the main centre of Orthodox Christian monasticism. The whole peninsula is a self-governing community of monks, where women are not allowed.

In antiquity it was known for wrecking a Persian fleet in 492 BCE, after which Xerxes had a canal dug across its neck. Hermits lived there by the 800s. In 963 Athanasius the Athonite founded the Great Lavra with the support of the emperor Nikephoros Phokas, and other houses followed. There are now twenty main monasteries, among them Georgian, Russian, Serbian and Bulgarian ones.

Athos shaped the Orthodox world. The monk Anthony brought its way of life to Kyiv, where he founded the Monastery of the Caves. The Serbian ruler Stefan Nemanja, founder of Studenica, ended his life there as a monk. In the 1300s its monks' practice of silent prayer, defended by Gregory Palamas, was at the centre of the Hesychast controversy. Under Ottoman rule the monasteries kept their self-government, and they still do under Greece.
sum: Mount Athos is a mountain on a long peninsula of northern Greece, and since the 900s the main centre of Orthodox Christian monasticism. The whole peninsula is a self-governing community of monks, where women are not allowed.
